metadata.title: Meta’s AI shopping push could lift Instagram ad revenue, Jefferies says

content.text:
Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META, XETRA:FB2A, SIX:FB) Muse assistant now handles Black Friday shopping at Walmart Inc (NYSE:WMT, XETRA:WMT), an example of the revenue opportunity Jefferies sees.
Jefferies, which has a "buy" rating and $875 price target, considers the stock undervalued at 8.5 times forecast 2027 EBITDA on an enterprise value basis, compared with an average of 13.3 times for peers.
The broker also sees room for Meta to exceed the consensus forecast of 17% sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter of 2026, below its pre-pandemic seasonal range of 19% to 26%.

Read more about Meta Platforms
Walmart shows how the shopping service works, with Muse finding deals, building a basket, and completing the purchase after the shopper approves it.
Jefferies cited Forter data showing Muse placed 49% of the AI agent orders Forter tracked in the first full week of November.
The broker's analysts also spotted a shopping option on a few Instagram Reels, where Muse found products linked by creators and offered viewers the option to buy.
Jefferies said the feature might help Meta turn more ad views into purchases and encourage advertisers to spend more on Instagram.
The assistant is now available in Singapore, Australia, and the UK, with plans to bring Muse to the company's glasses in Australia and the UK.
